# Factory coverage: implementation-ready, tests-only plan

## Scope and evidence

Target: `lib/zaq/agent/factory.ex`; supplied baseline **92%**, missed source lines **188, 194, 377, 451, 454, 477, 482, 490, 491**. Numbers below are one-based against the inspected 494-line working-tree file. The percentage is user-supplied, not freshly measured.

Planning only. No application/test implementation or validation was performed. This temporary document is the only authored artifact. No Git or Beadwork mutations are part of the plan or this planning session. Preserve all pre-existing dirty work. `bw prime` and a bounded existing-issue lookup were read-only; the user's explicit instruction to preserve the dirty tree resolves the generic dirty-tree prompt from `bw prime`.

**Action reuse assessment: N/A — tests only.** No executable application operation, Action, tool exposure, production dependency seam, or lifecycle behavior changes are proposed.

Read: `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agent-tools.md`, `docs/testing-approach.md`, `docs/services/agent.md` Factory/provider/lifecycle and harness-critical sections, `docs/services/system-config.md`, workflow planning/validation sections, setup and documentation policies. Loaded `test-coverage-planner`. Used Serena overview/definitions for Factory, ProviderSpec, Skills, ServerManager, AIRuntimeCredentials, and test helpers. Dependency-source symbol extraction was unavailable; bounded reads verified the relevant Jido APIs. Context Mode execution failed with `disk I/O error`; bounded reads/searches were used instead. No environment repair was attempted.

Scoped read-only Git status showed no existing changes in Factory, FactoryTest, ProviderSpecTest, AIRuntimeCredentialsTest, mocks, or system-config fixtures at inspection time. The checkout as a whole is dirty; recheck ownership before implementation without resetting/stashing anything. Existing relevant tracker context includes `zaq-jrg.27` / `.28` (global AI authentication cutover/validation); no new tracking changes are requested.

## 1. Exact ownership and sequence

| Work | File/module owning the change | Ownership constraints |
|---|---|---|
| C1 nil Engine response; C2 malformed responses; P1 guard property | **Edit** `test/zaq/agent/factory_test.exs`, `Zaq.Agent.FactoryTest` | Reuse its nested `RuntimeCredentialRouter`, aliases, actor, DataCase. Add `use ExUnitProperties` here for P1. Keep existing tests and assertions. |
| R1 missing native loaders; R2 failed loader inspection; R3 prompt retries; R4 unavailable prompt status | **Add** `test/zaq/agent/factory_runtime_failure_test.exs`, `Zaq.Agent.FactoryRuntimeFailureTest` | `use Zaq.DataCase, async: false`; local setup helpers and nested process-boundary proxy belong in this file. |
| Unreachable branch documentation | This handoff / coordinator's final coverage summary | Do not alter Factory or coverage-ignore configuration to force 100%. |

Order: C1/C2/P1 and runtime-test preparation are independent; runtime preparation precedes R1–R4; coordinator validation follows all test edits. This is an ownership map, not authorization to spawn agents.

### Shared provider/runtime-credential paths — coordinator coordination required

These are **read/reuse or regression-test paths, not edit ownership for this task**:

- `test/zaq/agent/provider_spec_test.exs`: already tests canonical versus legacy secrets, resolved Person authentication, selected Codex identity, and unsupported auth kinds. Do not duplicate provider matrices in Factory tests.
- `test/zaq/engine/connect/ai_runtime_credentials_test.exs`: already asserts a missing AI-provider ID (`0`) resolves to `{:ok, nil}`, validates actors, and verifies the secret-free provider projection.
- `test/support/system_config_fixtures.ex`: canonical AI/Connect fixture creation and explicit keyless metadata. Shared with provider/runtime-credential coverage work.
- `test/support/mocks.ex`: already defines `Zaq.NodeRouterMock`; do not add a second router mock or alter this shared file.
- `test/support/data_case.ex`, `test/support/openai_stub.ex`, `test/support/multi_agent_openai_stub.ex`: shared infrastructure. Reuse without changes.
- Production `provider_spec.ex`, `engine/connect/ai_runtime_credentials.ex`, System/Connect credential resolution and encryption paths: read-only dependencies.

Coordinate overlapping edits to `factory_test.exs`, too: that file already contains credential, provider, skill, and streaming coverage. Do not relocate existing provider assertions during this task.

## 2. Complete missed-line mapping

| Source line | Current branch | Scenario and exact observable result | Reachability |
|---|---|---|---|
| 188 (body 189) | Engine response `{:ok, nil}` | C1: lifecycle runtime succeeds without a selected credential dependency; matches equivalent no-credential lifecycle config | Reachable; Engine explicitly returns this for a missing provider row |
| 194 (body 195) | Unexpected Engine response | C2/P1: exact `{:error, {:invalid_runtime_credential_response, response}}` | Reachable through injected router boundary |
| 377 | Non-map context in `put_context_window/2` | Existing invalid-context test exercises upstream normalization; record this line as unreachable | Unreachable through current public call chain; proof below |
| 451 | Missing native skill loader(s) | R1: exact `{:error, {:runtime_sync_required, ["load_skill", "load_skill_resource"]}}`, then exact singleton missing-loader error | Reachable on a server with cached config whose tools lag attached skills |
| 454 (body 455) | `Jido.AI.list_tools/1` returns error | R2: exact `{:error, {:runtime_sync_check_failed, :not_found}}` after successful cached-config status read | Reachable at process boundary; deterministic fault injection needed |
| 477 (body 478) | Current system prompt status unavailable/nonmatching shape | R4: second state read fails, prompt update is attempted, eventual exact configuration-failure result | Reachable; do not fail the first status read |
| 482 | Retry budget exhausted | R3 and R4: exact `{:error, :system_prompt_config_failed}` after four rejected prompt-update signals | Reachable without private calls |
| 490 | Existing production 20 ms retry backoff | R3/R4 traverse on each failed prompt update | Reachable; test adds no sleeps or wall-clock assertion |
| 491 | Recursive retry | R3/R4 observe four matching prompt-update signals and final failure | Reachable; retry bound is the asserted contract |

Expected outcome: meaningful tests for **eight of nine** reported lines; one justified unreachable defensive branch. Do not promise an exact new percentage: executable-line accounting and other coverage runs may differ.

## 3. Existing infrastructure and behavior to preserve

### Factory tests and credential boundaries

`FactoryTest` already uses `Zaq.DataCase, async: false`, imports `Zaq.SystemConfigFixtures`, and defines `@execution_actor %{kind: :system, subject: "factory-test"}`. Its nested `RuntimeCredentialRouter.dispatch/1` reads the test process dictionary key `:runtime_credential_response`, returns the event with that response, and sends `{:runtime_credential_event, original_event, routed_event}` to the caller.

Existing lifecycle tests cover actor validation, real Person grant selection, required-policy rejection, unloaded associations, the confidential Engine event, and Engine-unavailable errors. C1/C2 target the two remaining response branches, not those already-covered contracts.

`ai_credential_fixture/1` creates through `Zaq.System.create_ai_provider_credential/1`; it generates a unique name and builds canonical Connect-backed authentication. Without a supplied nonblank key or explicit metadata it adds `%{"auth_kind" => "none"}`. Use fixture keys only, never ambient credentials or the legacy AI key as runtime authority. Test encryption is already configured by `config/test.exs`; do not change encryption application configuration.

### Runtime tests

Existing Factory tests cover normal asks, authoritative cached LLM options, prompt refresh, invalid tool-context normalization, native skill tools present, and missing cached runtime config. They do **not** make loader inspection fail after a successful status read, or exhaust prompt updates.

Reuse the direct real `Jido.AgentServer` startup pattern from FactoryTest's missing-runtime-config test. Keep the real Factory module, real Jido client functions, Skills and tool integration. The missing native loader names are verified in dependency source: `LoadSkill.name/0` is `"load_skill"`; `LoadResource.name/0` is `"load_skill_resource"`. `AgentIntegration.prepare/1` emits loaders in that order for nonempty skills.

`OpenAIStub.server/2` provides a supervised loopback Bandit child and `/v1` endpoint and emits `{:openai_request, method, path, query, body}`. Existing `streamed_reply/3` in FactoryTest supports successful streaming; the new rejection tests do not need to move or copy it. `ToolCallingLLMStub` and `IntegrationAgent` are unnecessary here: no tool call or full Executor journey is being tested.

### Mocks

No new Mox definitions or global Mox mode. Reuse `RuntimeCredentialRouter` for C1/C2/P1. The runtime failure scenarios use the narrow test-only process proxy described below, not module replacement of Factory, Jido.AI, Jido.AgentServer, Skills, ProviderSpec, or Connect. `Zaq.NodeRouterMock` is available if future scope requires it, but not needed in this plan. Any future use must match exact Events and use `verify_on_exit!`, not a blanket stub.

## 4. C1 — explicit nil runtime credential response

Suggested test name: `"lifecycle config accepts an explicit missing runtime credential response without using attached secrets"`.

1. Create an AI fixture with provider `"openai"`, endpoint `"https://factory-nil.invalid/v1"`, API key `"factory-nil-attached-secret"`.
2. Build `%ConfiguredAgent{job: "Nil credential inspection", model: "gpt-4.1-mini", enabled_tool_keys: [], enabled_skill_ids: [], credential_id: credential.id, credential: credential, advanced_options: %{"temperature" => 0.23}}`.
3. Set the existing process-local router response to `{:ok, nil}`. Call `Factory.runtime_config(agent, actor: @execution_actor, node_router_module: RuntimeCredentialRouter)`.
4. Assert `{:ok, runtime}`; exact prompt `"Nil credential inspection"`, `runtime.llm_opts[:temperature] == 0.23`, actor preserved both at `runtime.execution_actor` and `runtime.tool_context.actor`, and absence of `:credential_dependency`.
5. Assert `runtime.llm_opts[:api_key] != "factory-nil-attached-secret"` and `runtime.llm_opts[:base_url] != "https://factory-nil.invalid/v1"`. Do not assert that all API keys are absent: Factory merges system generation defaults, which may contain the configured global credential's key.
6. Compare the complete result with an otherwise identical agent whose `credential` and `credential_id` are explicitly nil, using the same lifecycle entry point and actor. This is the semantic equivalence invariant for the nil result, not a reimplementation of option-merging logic.
7. Consume exactly one `:runtime_credential_event`; assert credential ID, `next_hop.destination == :engine`, actor equality, `opts[:action] == :resolve_ai_runtime_credential`, `opts[:confidential] == true`, and returned response `{:ok, nil}`. Refute a second captured event (including from the no-credential control).

The association fixture deliberately exists even though the controlled response is nil: it detects accidental re-reading/fallback to attached authentication. Real-world reachability is separately established by existing `AIRuntimeCredentialsTest`'s missing-ID test. Do not describe this as a newly designed missing-credential authorization policy.

Process dictionary cleanup: values are process-local and die with the test. For a reused helper or multi-case loop, capture `Process.get/2` with an absent sentinel, set the response in `try`, then restore/delete in `after` **in the same process**. Do not rely on `on_exit` deleting another process's dictionary.

## 5. C2 / P1 — malformed Engine envelopes

Suggested example test: `"lifecycle config rejects malformed Engine credential responses verbatim"`.

Use `%ConfiguredAgent{credential_id: 73, job: "Rejected runtime", enabled_tool_keys: [], enabled_skill_ids: [], advanced_options: %{}}` with the default unloaded association and explicit actor. No fixture row for ID 73 is necessary: the injected router is the boundary, and this branch returns before configuration assembly/database work.

Concrete response table (all are deliberately secret-free):

- `:unexpected_response`
- `nil` (distinct from accepted `{:ok, nil}`)
- `{:ok, %{}}`
- `{:ok, %{credential: %{id: 73}, resolved_credential: nil}}`
- `{:ok, %{credential: "invalid-provider", resolved_credential: %{}}}`

For each input, set the process-local response, call public `runtime_config/2`, and assert exact equality with `{:error, {:invalid_runtime_credential_response, response}}`. Consume its one captured confidential Engine event and assert the ID/actor/action/destination/confidential fields as in C1. Use one clearly named table test or individually generated tests, preserving input in assertion diagnostics. No provider HTTP calls, real grant selection, or extra DB records are needed.

**P1 invariant:** when the response is a purported success with a map provider projection but a non-map resolved credential, Factory rejects it unchanged rather than building an authenticated runtime.

- Add `use ExUnitProperties` in FactoryTest; StreamData is already a dependency.
- Use `check all bad <- generator, max_runs: 25`.
- Generator: `one_of` containing bounded `integer(-5..5)`, `boolean()`, `string(:alphanumeric, max_length: 24)`, `list_of(integer(-5..5), max_length: 3)`, and `constant(nil)`; no maps and no unbounded terms.
- Wrap each generated value as `{:ok, %{credential: %{id: 73}, resolved_credential: bad}}`.
- Assert the same exact error and consume/assert the routed event within each iteration. Restore the dictionary in the same iteration; don't accumulate messages.

**Guard limitation:** `{:ok, %{credential: %{}, resolved_credential: %{}}}` passes Factory's map guard and then reaches `ProviderSpec.llm_opts/2`, which requires a real `%ResolvedCredential{}` for the non-nil case. Do not include that value in a test expecting line 194, claim universal malformed-response rejection, or change production validation to satisfy the property. This plan tests the present guard's contract only.

## 6. Runtime setup and deterministic process-boundary proxy

Keep runtime scenarios in the new `FactoryRuntimeFailureTest`, `async: false`. This confines serial execution to the process/database failure suite and uses the existing shared sandbox semantics for runtime/plugin descendants. The existing FactoryTest is already serial; do not change its async mode as collateral work.

### Common real backend setup

Use a small local helper only because R1–R4 all need the same real backend:

1. Start `OpenAIStub.server/2` with a handler returning a fixed `500` JSON error if unexpectedly invoked. Its existing request observation identifies an erroneous ask; no public provider endpoint may be used.
2. Create an AI credential with `provider: "openai"`, that loopback endpoint and dummy `api_key: "factory-runtime-test-key"` through `ai_credential_fixture/1`.
3. Build a ConfiguredAgent value (no need to persist an agent) with loaded credential and ID, model `"gpt-4.1-mini"`, job `"Original cached prompt"`, no enabled tools or skills, empty advanced options, and `model_max_context_tokens: 5000`.
4. Obtain a valid `model` with `ProviderSpec.build/1` and a real lifecycle `runtime_config` with `Factory.runtime_config/2`, using `%{kind: :system, subject: "factory-runtime-failure-test"}`. This uses canonical credential resolution and existing system defaults without global overrides.
5. Start a real `Jido.AgentServer` with `start_supervised!`, `agent: Factory`, `jido: Zaq.Agent.Jido`, `registry: Jido.registry_name(Zaq.Agent.Jido)`, a UUID-based **string** ID, and `initial_state` containing `model`, `runtime_config`, `execution_actor`, `tool_context` from the config, and `Jido.AI.Context.new()` as context. This mirrors inspected ServerManager spawning without involving its global singleton.
6. Ensure the backend prompt is `"Original cached prompt"` with the real public `Jido.AI.set_system_prompt/2`; this also establishes that the backend is ready. Do this before wrapping it in the proxy. No sleeps, registry polling or `:sys.replace_state`.

All server/HTTP/proxy processes are ExUnit-supervised. Use unique string IDs, no dynamic atoms or fixed globally registered test server names. Keep lifecycle/skill fixtures in the sandbox and let cleanup stop supervised children before the sandbox owner is released. No manually launched orphan Tasks, no ServerManager restart/stop-all operations. Use public stop plus a monitor only if implementation adds a process outside ExUnit supervision.

### Why a process proxy is necessary

Factory has no injected Jido client module. The error paths are failures of a separate agent-server process after earlier successful observations. An invalid server from the start returns `:missing_runtime_config` before the target lines. Killing a PID between calls is timing-dependent and can raise a `GenServer.call` exit instead of the tagged error being tested.

Add a small nested test-only `ScriptedServerProxy` implementing `GenServer`. It wraps a **real** backend and only controls the external process protocol used by unmodified Jido client functions:

- On `:get_state`, consume one explicit script entry. `:forward` means call real `Jido.AgentServer.state(backend)` and return its exact result. An error entry means return the specified `{:error, reason}` immediately. Never fabricate `%Jido.AgentServer.State{}` or strategy snapshots.
- On `{:signal, %Jido.Signal{type: "ai.react.set_system_prompt", data: %{system_prompt: prompt}}}`, send `{:prompt_update_attempt, unique_test_ref, prompt}` to the owner **before** replying with the configured error. No signal forwarding for R2–R4.
- Handle unexpected calls/casts by sending `{:unexpected_server_message, unique_test_ref, message}` and returning an explicit error for calls. Do not silently succeed or forward ask/subscribe operations.
- Fail/report a depleted state-read script rather than falling back to arbitrary behavior. This makes dependency protocol drift diagnosable.
- Do not add the helper under `lib/`, application configuration, global mocks, or production test flags. Keep its scope to transport failure simulation, not a parallel Factory implementation.

Verified dependency contract: `Jido.AgentServer.status/1` resolves the server, calls `:get_state`, requires a real `%State{agent: agent, agent_module: module}`, and computes the strategy snapshot. `Jido.AI.list_tools/1` separately calls `Jido.AgentServer.state/1`, which also uses `:get_state`. `Jido.AI.set_system_prompt/3` sends the exact signal above through `Jido.AgentServer.call/3`, whose wire call is `{:signal, signal}`. This is why forwarding actual backend state is important, and why a fake `:status` reply would not work.

The tests assert Factory's errors and public prompt-update attempts, not the contents/layout of private server state. Script order is setup required to place the fault at the external boundary. This is collaborator-contract fault injection, not proof of an actual scheduler race.

## 7. R1 — lagging native skill registration (line 451)

Test: `"ask rejects newly attached skills until their native loaders are registered"`.

1. Start the bare real backend above, which has valid cached runtime config but no native skill loaders.
2. Create a real skill with a unique valid slug, e.g. `"factory-sync-<positive-integer>"`, description `"Needs native loading"`, body `"Load these instructions when needed."`, and `provided_tool_keys: []`. Use `Skills.create_skill/1` (active defaults are exercised by existing tests).
3. Form a per-call ConfiguredAgent value from the base with `enabled_skill_ids: [skill.id]` and job `"Replacement skill prompt"`. Do not invoke RuntimeSync or ServerManager to update the server's tools: lag is the scenario.
4. Call `Factory.ask_with_config(backend, "hello", changed_agent)`. Assert exactly `{:error, {:runtime_sync_required, ["load_skill", "load_skill_resource"]}}`.
5. Use real `Jido.AI.register_tool(backend, LoadSkill)` and assert success. Call the same Factory API again. Assert exactly `{:error, {:runtime_sync_required, ["load_skill_resource"]}}`.
6. Publicly list backend tools and confirm `LoadSkill` is registered and `LoadResource` is not. Check backend status shows the original cached prompt is still effective; the failed preflight must not apply the replacement prompt.
7. Refute an observed `:openai_request`. Both calls must return an error, not a stream envelope. No actual load-resource invocation, tool mock or LLM completion is involved.

The two checks prove both complete and partial mismatch, including subtraction of already-registered tools; they do not calculate expected names from Factory's output. Existing skill-success tests supply the corresponding happy path.

## 8. R2 — native loader inspection fails (line 454)

Test: `"ask returns runtime sync check failure when tool inspection becomes unavailable"`.

- Reuse real backend and a real nonempty skill as in R1; the per-call agent has the skill enabled.
- Start proxy with state-read script `[:forward, {:error, :not_found}]`: the first read permits `server_runtime_config/2`; the second is real `Jido.AI.list_tools/1` attempting to inspect state.
- Call `Factory.ask_with_config(proxy_pid, "hello", changed_agent)`.
- Assert exactly `{:error, {:runtime_sync_check_failed, :not_found}}`.
- Refute `{:prompt_update_attempt, ref, _}`, `{:unexpected_server_message, ref, _}` and local HTTP observations after the synchronous call returns.

Do not substitute a missing server name or directly mock `list_tools`: neither establishes the intended public path correctly. A skill is mandatory; an empty skill list bypasses the inspection entirely.

## 9. R3 — exhausted prompt-update retry budget (lines 482, 490, 491)

Test: `"ask fails after four rejected system prompt updates and never starts generation"`.

- Base real backend, **no skills**. Per-call agent job is `"Replacement cached prompt"`, distinct from `"Original cached prompt"`.
- Proxy script `[:forward, :forward]`: first real state supplies cached config; second supplies the real original system prompt. Configure prompt signals to reply `{:error, :prompt_update_rejected}` immediately.
- Call `Factory.ask_with_config(proxy_pid, "hello", changed_agent)` and assert exactly `{:error, :system_prompt_config_failed}`.
- After return, consume exactly four `{:prompt_update_attempt, ref, "Replacement cached prompt"}` observations; `refute_received` a fifth and any different prompt under that reference. The retry count is a specified bounded recovery behavior, not incidental internal ordering.
- Refute unexpected proxy messages and any HTTP observation. Optionally verify real backend prompt remains the original through its public status API; the proxy did not forward updates.

Production already sleeps 20 ms on each failed update, including the last failure, so this test naturally incurs about 80 ms. It must not stub the clock, patch `Process.sleep`, add a test sleep, assert exact elapsed time, or wait five seconds per reply. The synchronous return and sent-before-reply attempt messages are completion signals. Keep this scenario `async: false` and comment that backoff belongs to the production path under test.

## 10. R4 — failed current-prompt observation (line 477 plus retry lines)

Test: `"ask attempts prompt recovery when current prompt status is unavailable"`.

- Base backend and per-call job `"Recover missing prompt"`, **no skills**.
- Proxy script `[:forward, {:error, :not_found}]`; unlike R2, the second read is now `current_system_prompt/1` because no native skill inspection occurs.
- Configure prompt signals to return `{:error, :not_found}` immediately.
- Assert exact final `{:error, :system_prompt_config_failed}` and four prompt-update observations containing `"Recover missing prompt"`; refute a fifth, unexpected messages and HTTP requests.

This proves the fallback returns nil and proceeds to best-effort prompt setting rather than incorrectly treating failed observation as an already-synchronized prompt. It is deliberately separate from R3 so normal stale-prompt retries and unavailable prompt status are independently protected. Successful prompt refresh remains covered by existing FactoryTest integration tests.

## 11. Line 377 — reachability proof and disposition

`put_context_window/2` is private, with its sole current caller in `ask_with_config/4`. Its immediate predecessor is `put_runtime_tool_context/2`:

1. With no skills, `skill_runtime_integration/1` returns `tool_context: %{}`.
2. With skills, verified `AgentIntegration.prepare/1` builds a map tool context (or returns an error and `with` stops).
3. `put_runtime_tool_context/2` merges a map caller context with that map, or replaces a non-map caller context with that map.
4. It writes the resulting map into the opts before `put_context_window/2` reads it.

Thus `tool_context: :invalid`, `nil`, a list, or a number cannot reach line 377; they hit the earlier fallback. Duplicate keyword inputs are likewise replaced by `Keyword.put` before the next stage. The existing test `"ask_with_config normalizes an invalid tool context before asking"` at current test line 635 already exercises the public normalization behavior.

**Disposition:** documented unreachable defensive branch under present contracts. Retain the existing normalization regression test. Do not call private functions, use BEAM instrumentation, replace AgentIntegration with an invalid return, mutate running state to impossible types, add a public wrapper, remove the guard, or add coverage exclusions. A future production change that makes upstream context non-map would invalidate this proof and require a new review.

## 12. Isolation, security, and acceptance checklist

- All calls under test are public `Factory.runtime_config/2` / `Factory.ask_with_config/4`; no private invocation or test-only production hook.
- No global environment edits, key rotation, persistent-term writes, shared registry resets, real provider requests or external credentials.
- Canonical fixture writes stay inside DataCase's sandbox; no direct plaintext credential inserts. No accidental assumption that nil Person permits privileged operations: explicit system actor is provided at lifecycle startup.
- The router fake returns only test-controlled, non-secret malformed terms; tests never log/serialize real `ResolvedCredential.authentication`. Successful credential translation/owner provenance belongs to the existing shared provider/Engine tests.
- New runtime cases are supervised, use unique string IDs, and have no sleeps/polling in tests. Shared sandbox mode is restricted to `async: false` suites. If a helper is later made async, explicitly allow every DB-using child PID rather than copying shared mode into an async test.
- Exact errors, native loader names, actor envelope and retry count are asserted. No weakening existing assertions, disabling tests or tagging these out as opt-in integration tests.
- P1 handles the broad malformed-envelope invariant. The runtime failure cases are concrete lifecycle side effects; a property enumerating timing/failure schedules would add complexity without improving these bounded contracts.
- Browser E2E is unnecessary: this is Factory contract/process coverage, with no new UI journey or System configuration behavior.
- Coverage disposition explicitly lists eight reachable lines and unreachable 377. No claim of a new measured percentage until the coordinator's separately authorized coverage stage.

## 13. Coordinator-only commands

Do not run commands during this planning task. After implementing the two owned test files, the **coordinator** runs only quality and targeted tests, sequentially, from the existing checkout with its configured test database. Route output through working Context Mode; if the disk-I/O problem persists, report the blocker or use an authorized bounded-output fallback, not a giant raw log dump.

```sh
mix q
mix test test/zaq/agent/factory_test.exs test/zaq/agent/factory_runtime_failure_test.exs test/zaq/agent/provider_spec_test.exs test/zaq/engine/connect/ai_runtime_credentials_test.exs
```

The two shared paths in the targeted command are regression coverage only; confirm with their coordinator/owner before overlapping file edits or test processes. Do not parallelize Mix commands against the same checkout/database. `mix test` already uses the test environment; its project alias creates/migrates the branch-derived test database, so the coordinator needs the usual DB prerequisites. No `--include integration` is required for the existing FactoryTest or the proposed suite.

If a targeted failure needs reproduction, rerun only its file/test line, preserving the reported seed; for example, substitute the actual post-edit test declaration line in:

```sh
mix test test/zaq/agent/factory_runtime_failure_test.exs:<actual-test-line> --seed <reported-seed>
```

Do not add full-suite, `mix precommit`, coveralls, coverup, standalone formatter, E2E, Git, or Beadwork mutation commands to this handoff's execution scope. `mix q` includes formatting and can touch pre-existing dirty files: the coordinator must inspect its effects and preserve unrelated work. No repeated broader validation after successful quality/targeted checks unless new edits or unresolved failures require it.

Acceptance report: owned files edited; C1/C2/P1/R1–R4 outcomes; quality and targeted-test results; line-377 exception; any Jido protocol/setup mismatch; and explicit statement that no production changes or shared helper rewrites were needed. Compilation/setup details of the proposed test-only proxy remain statically verified, not execution-proven, until those coordinator checks run.


Coordinator execution override: tests only in assigned files, preserve pre-existing edits; no worker Mix/Git/Beadwork mutations. Coordinator alone runs mix q and added/edited tests --cover. No full-suite or precommit execution for this coverage task.

Temporary display configuration restored. Keep remaining gaps/plan exceptions visible; no claim every line covered.
